A small, fluffy white puppy sits alone on a pale gray stone slab, its 
thick, cloud-like coat catching the soft light. The pup is very young, 
with a rounded head, short legs, and a pair of floppy ears—one of which 
droops gently over the side of its face. Its eyes are dark and glossy, its 
nose a small black button, and a few fine whiskers catch the light at the 
muzzle, where a faint smudge of darker shading marks the mouth. The 
puppy's body faces roughly toward the camera, but its head is turned to 
the side in a quiet, three-quarter profile, as though something just 
beyond the frame has caught its attention.

Around its neck is a thin red collar—a braided or beaded cord with a small 
knot and a round brass bell dangling from it, the only splash of color 
against the otherwise snow-white fur. The stone beneath the puppy is 
mottled and speckled, with a visible seam or edge running across the 
foreground, suggesting a step or ledge. Behind the pup, the background 
falls into deep, out-of-focus shadow, broken only by a horizontal band of 
warm tan, likely a wooden threshold, which keeps all the visual emphasis 
on the delicate, wide-eyed little dog.
